messages.content: What kind of fertilizer is best for growing tomatoes?

function.name: soil_analysis_analyze_soil_type

soil_type.description: The type of the soil. For example, loam, sandy, etc.

message.content: The best fertilizer for tomatoes depends on your soil’s current nutrient levels, but generally a balanced NPK (nitrogen-phosphorus-potassium) ratio works well. A common recommendation is a 5-10-10 or 4-8-8 blend, which supplies enough phosphorus for root development and potassium for fruit quality while keeping nitrogen moderate to avoid excessive leafy growth. If you’re using organic methods, composted manure or bone meal can provide slow‑release nutrients. Always test your soil first—if pH is low, add lime; if it’s high, use sulfur—to ensure optimal absorption.
